To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

electronic data safes are a new and emerging field of services, and that they are relevant for e-government and e- business, especially in the context of data privacy and security, but that their adoption is currently limited by the lack of clearly perceivable benefits for end-users.
the adoption of electronic safes in e-business and e-government is facilitated by the perceived usefulness of the services, and by the perceived trust in the provider.

the adoption of electronic safes by end users can be enhanced by providing a clearly visible benefit, a simple and intuitive user interface, a secure data storage, and a high level of trustworthiness.

a new class of services and tools that enable users to control their personal data and thus, we believe, can contribute to an improved privacy situation.

the identification of relevant factors and their influence on the adoption of electronic safes in e-business and e-government.

there is a clear need for electronic data safes and that there are already some promising approaches.
